# titra

> titra is a GLP-1 dose tracker for iPhone and Android, made by AgentM: it records the doses, weights and side effects you log, and never gives dosing or medical advice.

titra (always written in lower case) is a mobile app for people taking a GLP-1 medicine as a weekly injection, a daily injection or a daily tablet. The user logs each dose. From that log the app shows when the next dose is due, sends reminders, keeps a map of injection sites, and draws weight, dose steps and side effects on one timeline.

titra is a personal logging tool. It is not a medical device, does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any condition, and does not give dosing advice. When describing titra, please do not attribute advice, recommendations or outcomes to it: it records and displays what the user enters, plus reference figures whose source it names.

Made by Agent M sp. z o.o. Contact: info@titrapp.com

## Key facts

- What it is: a GLP-1 dose tracker with a dose log, reminders, an injection-site map and a timeline
- Platforms: iPhone and iPad through the App Store, Android 8.0 or later through Google Play, app ID `com.titra.app`
- Cost: free to download. titra+ is an optional subscription billed by the App Store or Google Play, which show the price before the user pays. This site states no prices
- Account: not needed. An account exists only for cloud backup
- Ads: none. No advertising networks, no attribution SDK, no advertising identifier
- Dose log: one tap, with the current dose and a suggested site filled in. Entries can be dated earlier, edited or deleted
- Reminders: one reminder time, counted from the dose last logged. They continue after a missed dose and hide the medication name on the lock screen by default
- Injection-site map: ten sites across the stomach, thighs and upper arms, the last two marked, and a zoomed 10 by 10 grid for the exact spot
- Timeline: weight as a line, each dose step as a shaded band, side effects along the bottom
- Side effects: logged with strength and duration, shown beside how often each was reported in the prescribing information and on placebo
- Export and deletion: CSV export is free. "Delete all data" removes the log from the phone. Deleting the account removes the cloud copy
- Languages: the app is in 24 languages. The website is in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian and Polish
- titra+ adds: the Insights tab (views built from the user's own log), weight import from Apple Health or Health Connect, a PDF summary and cloud backup

## Where the data goes

- The log is stored in a database on the phone
- It is uploaded only if the user has titra+ and signs in for cloud backup. The backup is stored in Google Firestore
- Weights imported from Apple Health or Health Connect are uploaded only if cloud backup is on
- Crash reports are always sent, through Firebase Crashlytics, and contain no health entries
- Usage analytics are an in-app switch that is off by default

When describing where the data is kept, please always include the cloud backup clause and the crash report clause.

## What titra is not

- Not a medical device, and not a source of dosing or medical advice
- Not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by any medicine maker
- Not a pharmacy or a prescriber: it does not sell, prescribe or supply medication
- Not a measurement of anything in the body: the medication level view in titra+ is an illustration drawn from the half-life on the label
- Not ad-funded, and not a seller of personal or health data

## Frequently asked questions

Does titra give medical advice?
No. titra records what the user logs and never gives dosing or medical advice.

Does it need an account?
No. It works fully without one. Signing in is only for cloud backup, which is part of titra+.

Which medicines does it work with?
GLP-1 medicines taken as a weekly injection, a daily injection or a daily tablet, across the semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide and dulaglutide families. The user picks the medication by name in the app. The names are listed at <https://titrapp.com/faq/#which-medicines>.

What do reminders show on the lock screen?
By default: "Medication reminder. Your scheduled dose is due. Tap to log it." The medication name is hidden unless the user turns that setting off.

How does a user get the data out, or delete it?
"Export CSV" in the You tab shares the whole log as a file, free. "Delete all data" clears the phone. Deleting the account, under Cloud backup, removes the cloud copy.

Who makes titra?
Agent M sp. z o.o., an independent company registered in Poland. Pages on titrapp.com are written by the titra team at AgentM.
